mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed responds to economic softening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings declines, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicates successful monetary policy response to economic softening, boosting corporate confidence and consumer spending to drive positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both decline in the last month
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market stabilization
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE decline in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market recovery regime defined by rising new housing starts and retail sales drives consumer spending growth, accelerating corporate revenue and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise in the last month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both rise in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in new housing starts indicates improving consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of broader economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where HOUST has been rising for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong labor market regime defined by robust job growth exceeding 100,000 new jobs per month, consumer spending and corporate revenue growth accelerate, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS monthly change exceeds 100.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in new housing starts and industrial production indicates broad-based economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both rise in the last month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO rise in the last month.
